title: Conditions Field Guide with the changing-weather sun-eye logo
scope: Visual mockup revision only; no website code or deployment changes.
prompt:
Create a realistic, production-quality edited website mockup from the two supplied images.

INPUT ROLES:
Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET: the selected Oregon Fish Forecast "Conditions Field Guide" homepage. Preserve its page structure, spacing, typography, navigation, section order, cream/blue/green/gold visual identity and existing content.
Image 2 is the EXACT NEW BRAND REFERENCE: the selected right-facing trout containing weather that changes from snow on the left through rain and clouds in the middle to sunshine on the right, with ONE gold sun also serving as the fish's eye. A branching cream Lake Billy Chinook-inspired cutout crosses its green landscape.

USER GOAL: Show this selected new logo on OUR EXISTING homepage mockup. This is one focused revision, not a new homepage concept.

TARGET DIMENSIONS: Match the full-page reference: portrait desktop webpage 1744 x 2336 pixels. Render the page itself with no browser frame, device, presentation board, headings outside the UI or extra mockup panels. Do not stretch or squash imagery or type.

BRAND PLACEMENT:
1. In the existing dark-blue masthead at top left, replace the old fish with the new weather fish from image 2. Use the fish mark alone beside the existing white horizontal two-line OREGON / FISH FORECAST wordmark, preserving the original readable header lockup. At a 1440px equivalent page scale, fish approximately 140px wide and total lockup approximately 350px. Thin warm-cream outer keyline to separate the blue fish boundary from the dark-blue masthead. Do not put the square cream source image into the header. No oversized header or competing wordmarks.
2. Replace the existing mountain-and-river illustration to the RIGHT of the headline with a large standalone NEW FISH MARK, about 520px wide at a 1440px equivalent page scale, aspect ratio preserved, centered in that existing illustration slot. Fish only; do not repeat the logo source's OREGON FISH FORECAST wordmark here. Blend its outside area seamlessly into the warm cream page. Preserve the actual distinctive silhouette, weather scene, cream branching lake and yellow sun-eye. This larger use must clearly show the transition SNOW on LEFT, RAIN/CLOUDS in CENTER, SUN at RIGHT EYE. No separate sun elsewhere.
3. Replace the old footer brand fish with a matching smaller version of the new mark, with cream keyline against the blue footer.
Use the actual supplied fish appearance consistently; do not invent another trout or generic mountain icon.

PRESERVE THE SELECTED PAGE:
- Blue masthead, navigation "The waters", "River conditions", "Our approach", small "CENTRAL OREGON PILOT".
- Cream hero with big left-aligned headline "Get to know the water." and existing paragraph "Landscapes change. Rivers move. This is your field guide to Oregon's key waters — and what to know before you go."
- Main Lower Deschutes panel and river photo; "Warm Springs to Trout Creek"; "First conditions page · Reach review in progress"; yellow primary button "Explore the Lower Deschutes".
- Three supporting columns: River flow, Weather, Sources. For accuracy, River flow copy should be "Validated gauge observations, with visible measurement times." Keep the other two columns consistent with reference.
- "More waters on the horizon." section, original river photo, list of Crooked River, Metolius River, Fall River, Haystack Reservoir, Lake Billy Chinook, all visibly marked "PROPOSED COVERAGE".
- Blue footer "The source matters. Our approach."

Style: strong bold readable sans-serif similar to DM Sans, generous whitespace, warm paper #F5F2E9, Oregon blue #002A86, evergreen #285D45, gold #FFEA0F. Maintain reference sizes and hierarchy. No extra cards, no additional features, no live metrics, scores, forecasts, invented conditions or new coverage claims. Current date anchor 2026-10-08; no dates need be added. Preserve the existing photography as mockup imagery. The revised brand is the only major visual change.
